record.paper_title: Minimal positive realizations: a survey of recent results and open problems
record.original_question: For a strictly proper rational transfer function G(z), a positive realization is a finite-dimensional triple {A, b, c^T} with A, b, and c^T entrywise nonnegative such that G(z) = Σ_{k≥1} c^T A^{k-1} b z^{-k}. The minimality problem asks for the smallest state dimension N among such positive realizations. Which mathematical framework should be used to attack this minimality problem effectively: should one work with invariant cones, or is another formulation such as positive factorization of the Hankel matrix the right tool for obtaining general minimality results beyond the already understood cases?

evidence.quote: The positive realization problem consists of providing answers to the questions: - (The minimality problem) What is a minimal value for N?
First of all, it is not clear what kind of mathematical "instruments" should be used to effectively tackle this problem.
A different formulation, such as the factorization approach proposed by Picci and van Schuppen in reference [30], can be a viable and promising possibility.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G(z) be a strictly proper rational transfer function with nonnegative impulse response, i.e., G(z) = Σ_{k≥1} h_k z^{-k} with h_k ≥ 0 for all k ≥ 1. A positive realization of G(z) is a triple {A, b, c^T} consisting of an N×N matrix A, an N×1 column vector b, and a 1×N row vector c^T, all with entrywise nonnegative entries, such that h_k = c^T A^{k-1} b for every k ≥ 1. The dimension of such a realization is the integer N. The minimality problem asks: determine the smallest dimension N (the minimal positive realization dimension) over all positive realizations of a given G(z), and provide a constructive procedure or general characterization for computing this minimum.

Concretely, develop a general framework — for instance, based either on invariant polyhedral cones containing the reachable set, or on nonnegative (positive) factorizations of the infinite Hankel matrix H = (h_{i+j-1})_{i,j≥1} of the form H = P Q with P, Q entrywise nonnegative — that yields necessary and sufficient conditions and an effective algorithm for determining the minimal positive realization dimension of an arbitrary strictly proper rational transfer function with nonnegative impulse response, beyond the special cases already understood.
artifact.category_tag: Positive linear systems and realization theory
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys and tutorials on the positive realization problem indicate that, while necessary and sufficient conditions for minimality in terms of positive factorizations of the Hankel matrix exist, no general procedure for computing the minimal positive realization dimension is available; the nonnegative rank of the Hankel matrix is only a lower bound, and cone-based and factorization-based approaches each have limitations. The problem remains open in general.
